hints: The kth lexicographic permutation is selected by its first-element block, then the next block.
There are (n-1)! permutations beginning with each available first value.
For ranking, count unused values smaller than each element and add their factorial-sized blocks.
analogy: Factorials tell how many dictionary-ordered permutations each next number skips.
algorithm: For unranking, convert k to zero-based, choose index k/(r-1)!, then set k %= (r-1)!. For ranking, add the count of smaller unused values times (r-1)! at each position and return one-based rank.
correctness: Lexicographic order groups permutations by next unused element, and each group has exactly (r-1)! arrangements; skipping those groups gives the exact rank or selection.
complexity: O(n^2) with a simple unused list (n<=20), or O(n log n) with an order-statistics structure; O(n) space.
example: For n=3, k=4: each first-number block has (3-1)!=2 permutations. Skip the first three permutations, choose 2 as the first value, and the remaining order is 3,1, so the result is 2,3,1.
